title: Identification of the Poincare pairing with Verdier duality
statement:
Fix $\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\Qlb\}$, the smooth
geometrically connected $k$-scheme $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$ of dimension $d$
(not necessarily proper), and its
structure morphism $a_X:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ as in
the Poincare duality conventions.
Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ be
perfect over $\Lambda_X$, with
coefficient dual $K^\vee$.
The tensor–internal-Hom adjoint of the
derived Poincare pairing is
the canonical isomorphism

$$
b_K^\sharp:R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]
\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(R\Gamma_c(X,K),\Lambda).
$$

Its inverse is the global Verdier-duality isomorphism followed by the
smooth-purity identification of the Verdier dual.

proof.text:
Work at the fixed coefficient stage and in [def-pod-conventions]; in particular $X$ is smooth, separated, geometrically connected and finite type of pure dimension $d$, $a=a_X$ is admissible, and $K$ is bounded constructible finite-Tor and perfect over $\Lambda_X$ ([def-pod-perfect-complex-on-x]). We identify point sheaf objects with their coefficient complexes using $F=\operatorname{Fib}_s$ of [def-weil-finite-coefficient-point], the exact equivalence [lem-weil-point-fibre-equivalence], and its coherent tensor and unit comparisons [lem-sf-point-fibre-derived-tensor]; occurrences of $F$ and these comparisons are suppressed below. Put $C=Ra_!K$, $\omega=Ra^!\Lambda$, $L=R\mathcal Hom_X(K,\omega)=\mathbb D_XK$, $D=Ra_*L$, and $H_s=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$ (initially abbreviated $H$). The finite-level preservation statements [thm-sf-ctf-stability] put $\omega,L$ in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $C,D,H$ in $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$: apply exceptional preservation to $\Lambda$, internal-Hom preservation to $(K,\omega)$, the two direct-image assertions to $K,L$, and internal-Hom preservation at $s$ to $(C,\Lambda)$. At integral coefficients the two direct-image membership assertions are [lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible] for $L$ and [lem-sf-integral-compact-support-constructible] for $K$; use [thm-sf-ctf-stability] (vii) to identify $D^b_c$ with $D^b_{ctf}$ and to preserve internal Hom and the exceptional adjoint. At field coefficients use the specified rationalization and common-stage constructions of the cited operations and the field clause of (vii). Here the sheaf object denoted by $H$ is $H_s=R\mathcal Hom_s(C,\Lambda_s)$; its coefficient interpretation is justified as follows, rather than assumed from essential surjectivity on a larger category. For any $U,V\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$ define
$$\kappa_{U,V}:F R\mathcal Hom_s(U,V)\longrightarrow R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FU,FV)$$
as the coefficient tensor–Hom transpose of $F(\operatorname{ev}_{U,V})$, precomposed with the inverse tensor comparison. For $T=\Lambda_s[-r]$, full faithfulness, the restricted tensor–Hom adjunction [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions], and tensor comparison give
$$\operatorname{Hom}(FT,F R\mathcal Hom_s(U,V))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(T,R\mathcal Hom_s(U,V))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(U\otimes T,V)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FU\otimes FT,FV)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(FT,R\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(FU,FV)).$$
By the defining transpose formula and the uncurry laws [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws], this bijection is exactly postcomposition with $\kappa_{U,V}$. Since $FT=\Lambda[-r]$ and the coefficient unit is free of rank one, these Hom groups are the degree-$r$ cohomology groups (a map from the single free module complex is a cycle modulo boundaries). Thus $\kappa_{U,V}$ is an isomorphism by [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology]. At algebraically closed coefficients make this calculation at a common finite field and then take its morphism class. Its evaluation compatibility is its defining equation
$$\operatorname{ev}^{\mathrm{coeff}}\circ(1_{FU}\otimes\kappa_{U,V})=F(\operatorname{ev}_{U,V})\circ\tau_{U,R\mathcal Hom_s(U,V)}^{-1},$$
where $\tau_{M,N}:F(M\otimes N)\xrightarrow{\sim}FM\otimes FN$ is the tensor comparison. In particular $\kappa_{C,\Lambda_s}$ identifies $FH_s$ with the displayed coefficient $H$ and carries currying to coefficient currying. Cohomology has only been used to prove invertibility of this specified comparison, not equality of two derived maps. We now suppress $F$, $\kappa$ and the tensor comparisons as announced. The comparison [thm-sf-dual-perfect], including its compatibility with evaluation, gives $\theta:D\xrightarrow{\sim}Q$, where $Q=R\Gamma(X,K^\vee(d))[2d]$. In the current definition [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product], the projection input is $Ra_*L=D$, and its point-valued cup map is exactly $F$ of the projection/counit composite, precomposed with the inverse tensor comparison just specified. Define $p:C\otimes^L_\Lambda D\to\Lambda$ by the mixed-support cup product of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product], evaluation $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}L\to\omega$, and the exceptional counit $\mu:Ra_!\omega\to\Lambda$. The evaluation of [def-pod-coefficient-dual-on-x] and the pairing definition [def-pod-derived-poincare-pairing] give $\beta_K=p\circ(1_C\otimes\theta^{-1})$: that definition explicitly identifies the normalized smooth trace at every coefficient stage with the exceptional counit through the orientation. Its finite-level trace is the composite of [def-pur-smooth-trace]; higher stages here use the all-stage pairing definition, not an extension of the finite-level trace statement. Write $b_D=\operatorname{curry}(p):D\to H$; the transpose laws [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] give $b_K^\sharp=b_D\circ\theta^{-1}$.

Take an arbitrary $T\in D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$, not just a shift of the unit. By [thm-sf-ctf-stability], $La^*T$ and $K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}La^*T$ lie in $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, so the projection formula applies to $(K,T)$ and the exceptional adjunction applies to its tensor product and $\Lambda$. The ordinary and exceptional adjunctions at all four coefficient stages are [fix-prop-adjunctions] (1), (2), with the exceptional functor of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. The restricted tensor–internal-Hom adjunction is [det-thm-sf-ctf-stability-adjunctions] (2), with the symmetry interchanging the tensor factors when needed. The operations are those of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Thus the adjunctions and the projection isomorphism [def-exchange-projection], [fix-prop-projection-formula] give a natural bijection $\Phi_T$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,D)
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(La^*T,L)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}La^*T,Ra^!\Lambda)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(Ra_!(K\otimes^L_{\Lambda_X}La^*T),\Lambda)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(C\otimes^L_\Lambda T,\Lambda)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_s(T,H).
\end{aligned}
$$
The first bijection sends $t$ to $\varepsilon_L\circ La^*t$, where $\varepsilon$ is the ordinary counit. The next sends it to evaluation against $K$, the third sends $e$ to $\mu\circ Ra_!e$, and the fourth precomposes with $P_T=\operatorname{PF}_{a,K,T}:C\otimes T\xrightarrow{\sim}Ra_!(K\otimes La^*T)$. The fifth curries, with evaluation and transpose laws [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. These are natural bijections on every test object in the stated category; no adjunction for ordinary uncompleted integral operations has been substituted for the completed one.

proof.text:
We identify the actual maps, using the mixed-support construction of [def-pod-mixed-support-cup-product], the natural projection isomorphism [fix-prop-projection-formula], the counit of [fix-prop-adjunctions], and the transpose laws [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws]. Let $e:K\otimes La^*D\to\omega$ be $\operatorname{ev}_{K,\omega}\circ(1_K\otimes\varepsilon_L)$, so $p=\mu\circ Ra_!e\circ P_D$ in point sheaf notation. By the current cup-product definition its coefficient version is $F(\mu\circ Ra_!e\circ P_D)$ precomposed with the inverse tensor comparison; the identifications fixed in Step 1 carry evaluation, currying and composition to these coefficient maps. For $t:T\to D$ put $e_t=e\circ(1_K\otimes La^*t)$. Naturality of the projection transformation gives
$$P_D\circ(1_C\otimes t)=Ra_!(1_K\otimes La^*t)\circ P_T.$$
Consequently the uncurried map in the Hom chain is
$$\mu\circ Ra_!e_t\circ P_T
 =\mu\circ Ra_!e\circ P_D\circ(1_C\otimes t)
 =p\circ(1_C\otimes t).$$
Currying and [lem-pod-closed-uncurry-laws] therefore give $\Phi_T(t)=b_D\circ t$ for every $T$. To prove invertibility explicitly, take $T=H$ and let $v=\Phi_H^{-1}(1_H):H\to D$. Then $b_Dv=1_H$. At $T=D$, injectivity of $\Phi_D$ gives $vb_D=1_D$, since $\Phi_D(vb_D)=b_Dvb_D=b_D=\Phi_D(1_D)$. These tests are allowed because Step 1 placed $D,H$ in $D^b_{ctf}(s,\Lambda)$. Thus $b_D$ and $b_K^\sharp=b_D\theta^{-1}$ are isomorphisms.

For the inverse identification, [lem-pod-global-duality-map-identification] specifies the tensor–Hom comparison by its actual projection/evaluation/counit transpose, identifies it with both [lem-sf-tensor-hom] and [fix-lem-tensor-adjunction], and states its relation to the exchange [fix-cor-verdier-exchange]. Its displayed formula for $\alpha_s$ is exactly the sheaf map $b_D$ computed above. With the point comparison $\kappa$ of Step 1 it therefore gives $\alpha=\kappa F\alpha_s=b_D$ in the suppressed coefficient notation. This identification uses the formula, not uniqueness of an unspecified canonical isomorphism. The point-dualizing identification is the evaluated map $j:F(D_sC)\to(FC)^\vee$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. The map-identification lemma states $j=\kappa F\rho$ and $g=Fe\circ j^{-1}=\alpha^{-1}$ for the global map of [thm-pod-global-verdier-duality]. Thus the cited statement, including its point-normalization equation, supplies precisely the needed identification of the global map. Hence $g=v$, and
$$(\theta g)b_K^\sharp=\theta(vb_D)\theta^{-1}=1_Q,\qquad
b_K^\sharp(\theta g)=b_Dv=1_H.$$
The inverse is therefore global Verdier duality followed by the smooth comparison $\theta$ of [thm-sf-dual-perfect]. No properness is used; all adjunctions and projection maps have the separated finite-type hypotheses, and smoothness is used only in $\theta$.
